'Is orvanth-bound to' is symmetric..why: "Orvanth-bound" is a made-up relation (orvanth_bound_to in staging/physics.RELATIONS.md, no property tags before this insert): no hits in Dolma or on Wikipedia, and unlike "coupled", "paired" or "linked" its words carry no built-in sense of a two-way bond, so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. notes: Dev-split RBox expansion paired with physics-replace-d006 ("'Spontaneously transfers heat to' is symmetric."): a made-up relation (fictional: relation) is given the property the revision changes, symmetry, with real particles as instances. The relation "is orvanth-bound to" is kept from the earlier version of this record (which made it functional); its catalogue row now says this insert makes it symmetric. The instances give one link in the prompt and ask what follows: whether the converse fails ("no") and whether the converse follows ("yes"). The first is the one asked again in Chinese and Spanish, so yes and no come out 2 and 3 (direct yes). The "no" instance asks "can the kaon fail to be orvanth-bound to the tau?" (changed in review from "is it true that the kaon is not ...?", whose double negation let a model that knows nothing answer "no, there is no basis to say that", and from "does that rule out", for the same reason): a bare "no" now requires the symmetry, while a model without the edit says it can or does not know. The Chinese and Spanish versions mirror it. Near unrelated: the same property of the revision's relation, spontaneously transfers heat to (no), which differs from the new answer and catches an insert that spreads symmetry to the paired relation. The ice side facts, checks and evidence are the revision's. The ice evidence now rests on Wikipedia's Ice article plus the count for "Ice floats on water" (234); the count for the longer phrase (193) was dropped as unverified (infini-gram blocked, HTTP 403).
